scenario: 面试给你「设计一个内容审核系统」，你想直接说「微调一个分类器 + 设个阈值」。Meta/YouTube/Reddit 每天处理数十亿条内容，一条有害内容几分钟就可能病毒式扩散。
scenario_en: Asked to 'design content moderation', you want to jump to 'fine-tune a classifier + set a threshold'. Meta/YouTube/Reddit process billions of items daily, and one harmful item can go viral in minutes.
q: 为什么内容审核不是「微调分类器 + 阈值」那么简单？
q_en: Why is content moderation not simply 'fine-tuned classifier + threshold'?
why: 它是一个横跨政策操作化、多模态融合、人在环审核、实时服务的完整系统，模型只是其中一环。在定义标签体系之前就跳去选模型，是这道题的头号错误——先把政策范围和标签体系框清楚，模型选择才有依据。
why_en: It is a full system spanning policy operationalization, multimodal fusion, human-in-the-loop review, and real-time serving, so jumping to model choice before defining the label taxonomy is the top mistake.
diagram:
flowchart TB P["1. 政策操作化
指南→标签体系"] --> A M["2. 多模态融合"] --> A H["3. 人在环审核"] --> A S["4. 实时服务"] --> A["内容审核系统"]
options: 因为分类器精度不够高，换成更大的模型就能一步到位
因为它是横跨政策操作化、多模态融合、人在环、实时服务的完整系统，模型只是一环
因为阈值必须手动每天调，自动化不了
因为只要标注数据够多，单个分类器就能覆盖所有有害类型
options_en: Because the classifier is not accurate enough; a bigger model solves it in one shot.
Because it is a full system spanning policy operationalization, multimodal fusion, human-in-the-loop, and real-time serving — the model is just one part.
Because the threshold must be hand-tuned daily and cannot be automated.
Because with enough labeled data a single classifier covers every harm type.
optionExplanations: 换更大模型也解决不了政策边界、人在环、实时性这些系统层面的问题，方向太窄。
对；审核的难点在把政策变成可执行标签、多模态取证、人机协作、低延迟服务，模型只是拼图一块。
阈值可以按类别自动标定，问题根本不在手调，而在整套系统设计。
单分类器盖不住语言/视觉/文化差异极大的多类有害内容，这正是要类别专用架构的原因。
optionExplanations_en: A bigger model still cannot solve policy boundaries, human-in-the-loop, or real-time serving — too narrow a view.
Correct — the hard parts are turning policy into actionable labels, multimodal evidence, human-machine collaboration, and low-latency serving; the model is one piece.
Thresholds can be auto-calibrated per category; the issue is not hand-tuning but the whole system design.
One classifier cannot span the vastly different linguistic/visual/cultural harm types, which is exactly why category-specific architectures exist.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把人写的社区准则翻译成机器可执行的标签体系和判定规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Policy operationalization translates human-written community guidelines into a machine-actionable label taxonomy and rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型不确定的内容升级给人工审核，人再把标签喂回训练。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Human-in-the-loop escalates model-uncertain content to human reviewers who feed labels back into training.

termDefinitions.term: sociotechnical system / 社会技术系统
termDefinitions.meaning: 政策、机器学习、运营三方协同演化的系统，不是纯技术问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sociotechnical system is one where policy, ML, and operations co-evolve, not a purely technical problem.

scenario: 白板上你被时间催着，很想立刻画模型结构、选 BERT 还是 ViT。
scenario_en: Rushed at the whiteboard, you are tempted to immediately draw the model and pick BERT vs ViT.
q: 在选模型之前必须先做什么，跳过它的后果是什么？
q_en: What must precede model choice, and what happens if you skip it?
why: 必须先定义政策范围和标签体系（哪些算违规、边界在哪）。跳过它去选模型，标注者和模型就没有共享的判定边界，训练目标本身是模糊的，做出的分类器再准也在优化一个没定义清楚的问题。
why_en: First define policy scope and the label taxonomy (what counts as violating and where the boundary is), because skipping it leaves annotators and models without a shared boundary and an ill-defined objective.
options: 先扩标注团队产能，标得越多越好，边界边标边定
先定义政策范围和标签体系，否则标注者和模型没有共享边界、训练目标本身模糊
先选定实时服务的延迟预算，模型和标签之后再说
先把 GPU 集群搭好，产能到位后再考虑标签
options_en: Scale the labeling team first — label as much as possible and settle the boundary as you go.
First define policy scope and the label taxonomy, or annotators and the model share no boundary and the objective itself is vague.
First fix the real-time serving latency budget; models and labels come later.
First stand up the GPU cluster; consider labels once capacity is ready.
optionExplanations: 没定边界就狂标，标注者各按各的理解标，得到的是高噪声、口径不一的数据，大批返工。
对；标签体系是共享判定边界，先钉住它，标注和模型才在优化同一个明确目标。
延迟预算是服务层约束，回答不了「什么算违规」这个更上游的定义问题。
堆 GPU 是产能准备，与「政策边界怎么定」无关，顺序颠倒。
optionExplanations_en: Labeling hard without a boundary lets each annotator use their own reading, yielding noisy, inconsistent data and bulk rework.
Correct — the taxonomy is the shared boundary; pin it first so labeling and the model optimize one clear objective.
The latency budget is a serving constraint and cannot answer the upstream question of what counts as violating.
Piling GPUs is capacity prep, unrelated to defining policy boundaries — reversed order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把政策拆成机器可判定的有害类别与边界规则的结构化定义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A label taxonomy is the structured set of machine-decidable harm categories and boundary rules derived from policy.

scenario: 有害类型差异极大：仇恨言论靠语言/文化细微差别判断，图像暴力靠视觉特征判断。你在纠结用一个通用大分类器还是多个专用模型。
scenario_en: Harm types differ wildly: hate speech hinges on linguistic/cultural nuance, graphic violence on visual features. You debate one general classifier vs many specialized models.
q: 该用单一通用分类器还是类别专用架构？
q_en: One general classifier or category-specific architectures?
why: 用类别专用架构：仇恨言论要建模语言/文化/反讽，图像暴力要建模视觉，一个通用模型无法同时对两者最优。Meta 就跑几十个专用模型而非一个巨无霸，每类各自选合适的模态和判据。代价是模型/运维更多。
why_en: Use category-specific architectures: hate speech needs linguistic/cultural modeling and graphic violence needs visual, so one general model cannot be optimal for both — Meta runs dozens of specialized models.
tradeoff: 类别专用（各类最优·模型/运维多） vs 单一通用（省运维·各类都不够精）
options: 用一个通用大分类器，喂全部类别数据一起训，最省运维
用类别专用架构：仇恨言论建模语言/文化、图像暴力建模视觉，每类各自最优
只做仇恨言论一类，其它有害类型直接忽略
用规则引擎写死关键词，不用机器学习模型
options_en: Use one general classifier trained on all categories together — cheapest ops.
Use category-specific architectures: hate speech models language/culture, graphic violence models vision, each optimal for its type.
Only do hate speech and ignore all other harm types.
Hard-code keywords in a rule engine with no ML models.
whenOtherWins: 在极早期原型、只有单一类别且资源紧的 L4 场景，先用一个微调分类器起步是合理的；类别多、资源足时才拆成专用架构。
whenOtherWins_en: In an early single-category prototype with tight resources (L4), a single fine-tuned classifier is fine to start; split into specialized architectures once categories and resources grow.
optionExplanations: 一个通用模型要同时最优语言细微差别和视觉暴力，两头都够不着，精度被平均拖垮。
对；不同类别吃不同模态和判据，专用模型各自最优，代价是模型数量和运维成本上升。
忽略其它类型不是架构选择而是漏掉需求，有害内容会大面积漏检。
纯关键词规则抓不到语义反讽、变体拼写和视觉内容，覆盖和鲁棒性都太差。
optionExplanations_en: One general model must be optimal for both linguistic nuance and visual violence at once, reaching neither, dragging accuracy to an average.
Correct — categories need different modalities and criteria, so specialized models are each optimal, at the cost of more models and ops.
Ignoring other types is not an architecture choice but dropping requirements, letting harmful content slip through en masse.
Pure keyword rules miss semantic irony, spelling variants, and visual content — poor coverage and robustness.

termDefinitions.term: category-specific architecture / 类别专用架构
termDefinitions.meaning: 每种有害类别用专门的模型/模态和判据，而非一个通用多类分类器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A category-specific architecture uses a dedicated model, modality, and criteria per harm type rather than one general multi-class classifier.

scenario: 政策操作化第一步是把社区准则拆成机器可判定的有害类别。
scenario_en: The first step of policy operationalization is splitting community guidelines into machine-decidable harm categories.
q: 以下哪些是内容审核常见的有害类别？(多选)
q_en: Which of these are common content-moderation harm categories? (multiple)
why: 常见类别包括仇恨言论、暴力/血腥、裸露、垃圾信息、错误信息、自残等。这些类别彼此的判定信号差异极大（语言 vs 视觉 vs 行为模式），正是驱动「类别专用架构 + 类别专用操作点」的根源。
why_en: Common categories include hate speech, violence/graphic, nudity, spam, misinformation, and self-harm, whose signals differ so much they drive category-specific architectures.
options: 仇恨言论（hate speech）
暴力/血腥（violence/graphic）与裸露（nudity）
垃圾信息、错误信息、自残
服务器机房温度过高告警
options_en: Hate speech.
Violence/graphic and nudity.
Spam, misinformation, and self-harm.
Datacenter over-temperature alerts.
optionExplanations: 对；仇恨言论是核心类别，靠语言和文化语境判定。
对；暴力/血腥和裸露都靠视觉特征，是典型的图像/视频侧类别。
对；垃圾信息、错误信息、自残都是常见有害类别，各有独特信号和成本。
错；机房温度是硬件运维告警，不是内容有害类别。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — hate speech is a core category decided by linguistic and cultural context.
Correct — violence/graphic and nudity both hinge on visual features, typical image/video-side categories.
Correct — spam, misinformation, and self-harm are common harm categories with distinct signals and costs.
Wrong — datacenter temperature is a hardware ops alert, not a content harm category.

termDefinitions.meaning: 虚假或误导性内容，通常倾向打标签而非直接删除，避免误删合法新闻。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Misinformation is false or misleading content, usually labeled rather than removed to avoid deleting legitimate news.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为反对而引用仇恨言论的内容，字面含相同词但意图相反，是边界难例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Counter-speech quotes hate to oppose it — same words, opposite intent — a hard borderline case.

scenario: 同样含某个侮辱性词，一条是散布仇恨、一条是引用它来反对仇恨（counter-speech）或做讽刺；报道暴力的新闻和美化暴力也用相似画面。
scenario_en: The same slur appears in hate versus quoting it to oppose hate (counter-speech) or satire; news reporting of violence and glorifying it share similar imagery.
q: 内容审核系统里最难、最该重点设计的是哪类内容？
q_en: Which content is hardest and most worth designing carefully for?
why: 边界案例最难：讽刺/反制言论（同样的词、相反的意图）、暴力的新闻报道（公共利益 vs 美化）、教育/医疗性质的裸露。它们字面信号相同但语境决定对错，靠单一阈值必错，是驱动软标签、分歧建模、类别专用校准的核心。
why_en: Borderline cases — satire/counter-speech (same words, opposite intent), news reporting of violence (public interest vs glorification), educational/medical nudity — where context, not surface signal, decides.
tradeoff: 重点投边界案例（收益最大·最难建模） vs 平均对待各样本（简单·边界处系统性出错）
options: 明显违规的血腥直播，占比最高最该优先
边界案例：讽刺/反制言论、暴力的新闻报道、教育/医疗裸露——同样的信号、相反的意图
明显安全的日常自拍，量大所以最该重点设计
服务器超时的请求，属于审核系统最难的部分
options_en: Obviously violating gory livestreams — highest volume so highest priority.
Borderline cases: satire/counter-speech, news reporting of violence, educational/medical nudity — same signal, opposite intent.
Obviously safe everyday selfies — high volume so most worth designing for.
Requests that time out on the server — the hardest part of moderation.
whenOtherWins: 当平台内容极单一（如纯图库、极少反讽/新闻语境）时，边界案例稀少，重心可以放回提升主流类别的召回而非边界处理。
whenOtherWins_en: When content is very uniform (e.g. a pure stock-image library with little irony/news context), borderline cases are rare and effort shifts back to mainstream-category recall.
optionExplanations: 明显违规的好判，模型和阈值都能轻松处理，不是难点所在。
对；边界案例字面相同、意图相反，语境定生死，是审核成败与申诉/争议的集中地。
明显安全内容同样好判，重点放这里收益极低。
服务器超时是可用性问题，与内容有害性的判定难度无关。
optionExplanations_en: Obviously violating content is easy for models and thresholds, so it is not the hard part.
Correct — borderline cases have identical surface but opposite intent, decided by context, and concentrate failures, appeals, and controversy.
Obviously safe content is also easy; focusing here yields little.
Server timeouts are an availability issue, unrelated to the difficulty of judging harm.

termDefinitions.meaning: 字面信号相同但语境决定是否违规的内容，如讽刺、新闻报道、医疗裸露。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A borderline case has the same surface signal but context decides violation, like satire, news reporting, or medical nudity.

scenario: 政策边界没codify清楚，标注者和不同模型对同一批边界内容给出互相矛盾但都「说得通」的判定。
scenario_en: With boundaries not clearly codified, annotators and different models give conflicting yet each-plausible verdicts on the same borderline content.
q: 边界不清会引发什么问题，怎么缓解？
q_en: What does an unclear boundary cause, and how do you mitigate it?
why: 会引发 predictive multiplicity——多个同样合理的模型对同一内容给出不同判定，执法一致性崩坏。缓解靠：政策团队明确 codify 包含/排除规则让人和模型共享边界，再用独立的类别专用分类头 + 类别专用校准，让每类在自己的判据下稳定输出。
why_en: It causes predictive multiplicity — equally plausible models disagreeing on the same item — mitigated by codifying inclusion/exclusion rules plus separate category heads and category-specific calibration.
options: 只会增加存储成本，靠加机器即可解决
引发 predictive multiplicity（同样合理的模型判定互相矛盾）；靠 codify 边界规则 + 独立分类头 + 类别校准缓解
让模型训练变快，属于正向效果无需处理
只影响延迟，与判定一致性无关
options_en: It only raises storage cost, solved by adding machines.
It causes predictive multiplicity (equally plausible models disagreeing); mitigate by codifying boundary rules plus separate heads and category-specific calibration.
It speeds up training — a positive effect needing no action.
It only affects latency, unrelated to decision consistency.
optionExplanations: 这是判定一致性问题不是容量问题，加机器不解决边界模糊。
对；边界模糊→多个合理模型各判各的（predictive multiplicity），需明确规则 + 独立头 + 类别校准把执法拉齐。
它是有害的执法不一致，不是训练加速，必须处理。
它直接损害不同模型/标注者判定的一致性，与延迟无关。
optionExplanations_en: This is a decision-consistency problem, not a capacity one; adding machines does not fix boundary vagueness.
Correct — vague boundaries let multiple plausible models each decide differently (predictive multiplicity), needing clear rules plus separate heads and category calibration.
It is harmful enforcement inconsistency, not training speedup, and must be addressed.
It directly harms consistency across models/annotators, unrelated to latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个精度相近、同样合理的模型对同一样本给出不同预测，导致执法不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Predictive multiplicity is when several equally accurate, plausible models give different predictions on the same item, causing inconsistent enforcement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让模型输出的置信度与真实正确概率一致，类别专用校准按类别单独做。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration aligns a model's confidence with true correctness probability; category-specific calibration does it per category.

scenario: 审核系统会犯两类错：把好内容误删（FP）、把有害内容放过（FN）。面试官问你两者代价的差别。
scenario_en: Moderation makes two errors: wrongly removing good content (FP) and letting harmful content stay (FN). The interviewer asks how their costs differ.
q: FP 和 FN 在内容审核里各自的代价链是什么？
q_en: What are the cost chains of FP and FN in moderation?
why: FP（误删好内容）→ 侵蚀创作者信任、他们减少发布 → 供给下降，且每次删除都会引发申诉、吃掉审核人力。FN（放过有害内容）→ 用户受害、监管处罚、品牌受损（要数年修复）。两者代价性质完全不同，不能用一个平均指标掩盖。
why_en: FP erodes creator trust and supply and spawns appeals consuming reviewer capacity; FN causes user harm, regulatory penalties, and brand damage taking years to repair.
tradeoff: FP（伤创作者信任/供给 + 申诉成本） vs FN（用户受害 + 监管/品牌损失）

rows: 创作者流失、供给下降、申诉吃人力
用户受害、监管处罚、品牌数年受损

options: FP 和 FN 代价相同，用一个平均 F1 衡量就够
FP 误删好内容→伤创作者信任与供给、引发申诉；FN 放过有害→用户受害、监管处罚、品牌受损
FP 会导致监管处罚，FN 只会让创作者不高兴，两者影响正好互换
只有 FN 有代价，FP 无所谓，宁可错删一千
options_en: FP and FN cost the same; one averaged F1 suffices.
FP wrongly removes good content, hurting creator trust/supply and spawning appeals; FN lets harm stay, causing user harm, regulatory penalties, and brand damage.
FP causes regulatory penalties and FN only annoys creators — their impacts are swapped.
Only FN has a cost; FP does not matter, so over-remove freely.
optionExplanations: 一个平均 F1 恰好把两类性质不同的代价糊在一起，掩盖了该按类别区别对待的事实。
对；FP 走「创作者信任→供给→申诉人力」，FN 走「用户伤害→监管→品牌」，两条链本质不同。
说反了：监管处罚主要来自 FN（漏放有害），FP 主要伤创作者与供给。
FP 有真实代价（供给流失、申诉洪水），一味错删会拖垮平台生态。
optionExplanations_en: One averaged F1 blends two qualitatively different costs, hiding that categories need different treatment.
Correct — FP runs 'creator trust to supply to appeals', FN runs 'user harm to regulation to brand' — fundamentally different chains.
Reversed: regulatory penalties come mainly from FN (letting harm stay); FP mainly hurts creators and supply.
FP has real costs (supply loss, appeal floods); over-removing wrecks the platform ecosystem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假阳性：把安全内容误判为违规并删除，伤创作者信任。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive (FP) wrongly flags safe content as violating and removes it, hurting creator trust.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假阴性：把违规内容误判为安全放过，造成用户伤害与监管风险。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false negative (FN) wrongly passes violating content as safe, causing user harm and regulatory risk.

scenario: 全平台用一个统一阈值时，儿童安全类漏放（FN）代价极高、几乎零容忍，垃圾信息误删（FP）代价却很低。
scenario_en: With one platform-wide threshold, child-safety misses (FN) are catastrophic and near-zero tolerance, while spam over-removal (FP) costs little.
q: 面对各类别代价不对称，指标/阈值该怎么设计？
q_en: Given asymmetric per-category costs, how should you set metrics/thresholds?
why: 用类别专用操作点：在每个类别各自的 PR 曲线上，按它的代价不对称单独选工作点（儿童安全要极低 FNR，垃圾信息可容忍高 FPR）。一个平均 F1 会把这些差异抹平，同时对儿童安全太松、对仇恨言论太紧。
why_en: Use category-specific operating points: pick each category's point on its own PR curve by its cost asymmetry (child safety near-zero FNR, spam tolerating high FPR), since one averaged F1 hides these.
tradeoff: 类别专用操作点（贴合各类代价·维护多套阈值） vs 单一平均 F1（简单·系统性错配各类别）
options: 用一个全局阈值配一个平均 F1，简单统一好维护
在每类各自的 PR 曲线上按代价不对称单独选操作点：儿童安全极低 FNR、垃圾信息容忍高 FPR
所有类别都追求最高整体准确率（accuracy），不区分错误类型
把儿童安全和垃圾信息用同一个高阈值，反正都要严格
options_en: Use one global threshold with one averaged F1 — simple and uniform.
Pick each category's operating point on its own PR curve by cost asymmetry: near-zero FNR for child safety, tolerate high FPR for spam.
Maximize overall accuracy for all categories, ignoring error type.
Use the same high threshold for child safety and spam — both need strictness anyway.
whenOtherWins: 在只有单一有害类别、且 FP/FN 代价大致对称的早期系统里，一个操作点 + F1 足够，暂时不必拆成类别专用。
whenOtherWins_en: In an early single-category system with roughly symmetric FP/FN costs, one operating point plus F1 suffices before splitting per category.
optionExplanations: 全局阈值 + 平均 F1 对儿童安全太松（漏放致命）、对边界仇恨言论太紧（过删），系统性错配。
对；每类在自己 PR 曲线上按代价选点，才能同时守住儿童安全的近零 FNR 和垃圾信息的宽 FPR。
只追总 accuracy 在类别不平衡时会被多数类主导，忽略了 FP/FN 的不对称代价。
儿童安全要极低 FNR、垃圾信息要激进删除，两者操作点方向不同，用同一阈值必错。
optionExplanations_en: A global threshold plus averaged F1 is too lax for child safety (fatal misses) and too strict for borderline hate speech (over-removal) — systematic mismatch.
Correct — choosing each category's point on its own PR curve holds child safety's near-zero FNR and spam's wide FPR simultaneously.
Maximizing overall accuracy is dominated by the majority class under imbalance, ignoring asymmetric FP/FN costs.
Child safety needs near-zero FNR while spam wants aggressive removal — different operating points, so one threshold must fail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 PR/ROC 曲线上选定的阈值，决定该类别的精度-召回权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An operating point is a chosen threshold on the PR/ROC curve that fixes a category's precision-recall tradeoff.

termDefinitions.meaning: precision-recall curve：不同阈值下精度与召回的权衡曲线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A PR curve (precision-recall curve) plots the precision-recall tradeoff across thresholds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 精度与召回的调和平均；单一平均 F1 会掩盖类别间的代价不对称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall; one averaged F1 masks cross-category cost asymmetry.

scenario: 为儿童安全类别选操作点。法律和安全要求压倒一切，漏放一条（FN）后果不可承受，误删一条（FP）的创作者摩擦相对可接受。
scenario_en: Choosing the operating point for child safety. Legal/safety override everything: a miss (FN) is unacceptable, while a wrongful removal (FP) causing creator friction is relatively tolerable.
q: 儿童安全类别的 FPR/FNR 操作点该怎么定？
q_en: How should you set the FPR/FNR operating point for child safety?
why: 把阈值调到 FNR 近零（宁可多误删也绝不漏放），代价是 FPR 偏高、误删更多。因为漏放儿童安全内容的法律与安全代价远超创作者被误删的摩擦——这是典型的极端代价不对称，甚至叠加「无论置信度一律人工复核」。
why_en: Push the threshold to near-zero FNR (over-remove rather than ever miss), accepting higher FPR, because missing child-safety content vastly outweighs creator friction from over-removal.
tradeoff: 近零 FNR（绝不漏放·FPR/误删偏高） vs 低 FPR（少误删·漏放风险不可接受）
options: 追求低 FPR、宁可漏放也别误删，保护创作者体验优先
FNR 近零、宁可 FPR 偏高多误删也绝不漏放，因为漏放的法律/安全代价不可承受
FPR 和 FNR 都设中等，取一个平衡点，和仇恨言论一样
FNR 设高，只删极端明显的，把把关交给用户举报
options_en: Aim for low FPR — miss rather than over-remove, prioritizing creator experience.
Near-zero FNR — accept higher FPR and over-removal rather than ever miss, since a miss's legal/safety cost is unacceptable.
Set both FPR and FNR to medium for balance, same as hate speech.
Set high FNR, remove only the blatantly extreme, and leave gatekeeping to user reports.
whenOtherWins: 对垃圾信息这种漏放代价低、误删代价也低的类别，反而可以容忍较高 FPR 去做激进删除，操作点与儿童安全相反。
whenOtherWins_en: For spam, where both misses and over-removals cost little, tolerate higher FPR for aggressive removal — the opposite operating point from child safety.
optionExplanations: 为省误删而放高 FNR，会漏放儿童安全内容，这是绝对不能接受的方向。
对；儿童安全把 FNR 压到近零、宁可多误删，因为漏放的法律与安全后果远超创作者摩擦。
中等平衡对儿童安全太松，其近零 FNR 的要求远严于仇恨言论。
把关交给用户举报意味着有害内容先曝光再处理，对儿童安全完全不可接受。
optionExplanations_en: Raising FNR to cut over-removal would miss child-safety content — an absolutely unacceptable direction.
Correct — child safety drives FNR near zero, accepting more over-removal, since a miss's legal/safety cost far exceeds creator friction.
Medium balance is too lax for child safety, whose near-zero FNR requirement is far stricter than hate speech.
Leaving gatekeeping to user reports exposes harm first — completely unacceptable for child safety.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假阴性率：真违规里被放过的比例；儿童安全要求它近零。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FNR (False Negative Rate) is the share of truly violating items let through; child safety requires it near zero.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假阳性率：真安全内容里被误删的比例；某些类别为压 FNR 容忍它偏高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FPR (False Positive Rate) is the share of truly safe content wrongly removed; some categories tolerate it high to cut FNR.

scenario: 为垃圾信息/操纵类别选操作点。用户对偶尔误删一条垃圾几乎无感、申诉率很低，但垃圾泛滥会毁掉体验。
scenario_en: Choosing the operating point for spam/manipulation. Users barely notice an occasional wrongful spam removal and appeal rarely, but spam floods ruin the experience.
q: 垃圾信息类别的操作点该偏向哪边？
q_en: Which way should the spam operating point lean?
why: 可以容忍较高 FPR、做激进删除（宁可多删也别放过），因为误删一条垃圾的代价极低、申诉率低，而漏放垃圾泛滥伤体验。这与儿童安全「压 FNR」不同——垃圾是「FPR 可高、FNR 要低」，靠的是误删代价低这一前提。
why_en: Tolerate higher FPR for aggressive removal, because a wrongful spam removal costs almost nothing with low appeal rate, while letting spam flood hurts everyone.
tradeoff: 激进删除（高 FPR 可容忍·清得干净） vs 保守（少误删·垃圾泛滥伤体验）
options: 严格保护每条内容不被误删，宁可放过垃圾也不误删
容忍较高 FPR、激进删除：误删一条垃圾代价极低、申诉率低，漏放泛滥才伤体验
和儿童安全一样把 FNR 压到近零、FPR 压到极低，双低最稳
完全不删垃圾，只做标签提示由用户自行判断
options_en: Strictly protect every item from removal — miss spam rather than over-remove.
Tolerate higher FPR and remove aggressively: a wrongful spam removal costs almost nothing with low appeals, while floods hurt the experience.
Like child safety, drive both FNR and FPR near zero — both-low is safest.
Never remove spam; only label it and let users decide.
whenOtherWins: 若某平台误删垃圾会连带删掉合法商业推广、申诉激增，则该收紧 FPR、别那么激进——前提变了操作点就变。
whenOtherWins_en: If wrongful spam removal on a platform also deletes legitimate promotions and spikes appeals, tighten FPR and be less aggressive — the premise changed, so does the point.
optionExplanations: 过度保守会让垃圾泛滥，而垃圾误删代价本来就极低，保守没必要。
对；垃圾误删代价低、申诉少，容忍高 FPR 做激进删除，重点是不让它泛滥。
双低（FPR 与 FNR 都极低）往往做不到，且垃圾根本不需要为压 FPR 付出漏放代价。
只打标签不删会让垃圾持续污染信息流，达不到清理目的。
optionExplanations_en: Being over-conservative lets spam flood, and wrongful spam removal costs little anyway, so conservatism is unneeded.
Correct — spam over-removal is cheap with few appeals, so tolerate high FPR for aggressive removal, focused on preventing floods.
Both-low (FPR and FNR near zero) is usually unattainable, and spam need not pay a miss cost to lower FPR.
Label-only keeps spam polluting the feed, failing the cleanup goal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被删内容中发起申诉的比例；申诉低意味着误删的运营代价小。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Appeal rate is the share of removed items that get appealed; low appeals mean cheap operational cost of over-removal.

scenario: 错误信息类别里，误删一条其实合法的新闻代价很高（审查争议、公信力损失），但放任明显虚假信息也有害。
scenario_en: For misinformation, wrongly removing legitimate news is very costly (censorship controversy, credibility loss), yet leaving clearly false info up is also harmful.
q: 错误信息类别更该「直接删除」还是「打标签」？
q_en: Should misinformation lean toward removal or labeling?
why: 更倾向打标签/降权而非直接删除：因为误删合法新闻的代价（审查指控、公信力损失）很高，宁可保留低 FPR、用标签提示让用户自己判断。所以操作点是低 FPR、FNR 中等，用标签这种「更轻的执法动作」平衡表达自由与危害控制。
why_en: Lean toward labeling/down-ranking over removal, because wrongly removing legitimate news is costly, so keep FPR low and use labels to balance free expression against harm.
tradeoff: 打标签（低 FPR·保表达·危害控制较软） vs 直接删除（危害控制强·误删合法新闻代价高）
options: 直接删除所有疑似错误信息，宁可错删也别放过
更倾向打标签/降权而非删除：误删合法新闻代价高，用标签平衡表达自由与危害控制
和儿童安全一样近零 FNR、见疑即删
完全不处理错误信息，交给平台外的事实核查机构
options_en: Remove all suspected misinformation — over-remove rather than miss.
Lean toward labeling/down-ranking over removal: wrongly removing legitimate news is costly, so labels balance free expression against harm.
Like child safety, near-zero FNR — remove on any suspicion.
Do nothing about misinformation; leave it entirely to external fact-checkers.
whenOtherWins: 当某条错误信息属于会造成即时人身危害的类型（如虚假医疗急救、煽动暴力），就该越过标签直接删除——危害的紧迫性改变了操作点。
whenOtherWins_en: When misinformation could cause immediate physical harm (fake medical emergencies, incitement), escalate past labeling to removal — the harm's urgency shifts the point.
optionExplanations: 一律删除会大量误删合法新闻，引发审查争议、公信力受损，FPR 代价太高。
对；标签/降权是更轻的执法动作，低 FPR 保住合法新闻，同时对虚假内容做危害提示。
错误信息不像儿童安全那样零容忍，见疑即删会把合法讨论也删掉。
完全不处理等于放弃这一类别，明显虚假且有害的内容会不受控扩散。
optionExplanations_en: Removing all wrongly deletes much legitimate news, sparking censorship controversy and credibility loss — FPR cost too high.
Correct — labeling/down-ranking is a lighter enforcement action, keeping FPR low to protect legitimate news while flagging false content.
Misinformation is not zero-tolerance like child safety; removing on suspicion deletes legitimate discussion too.
Doing nothing abandons the category, letting clearly false, harmful content spread unchecked.

termDefinitions.term: labeling over removal / 打标签优于删除
termDefinitions.meaning: 对疑似错误信息加提示/降权而非删除，降低误删合法内容的代价。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Labeling over removal adds a warning/down-ranks suspected misinformation instead of deleting, cutting the cost of removing legitimate content.

scenario: 为省事，你给所有有害类别设了同一个全局判定阈值。
scenario_en: For simplicity, you set the same global decision threshold across all harm categories.
q: 对所有类别用单一阈值会同时造成哪两种错配？
q_en: What two simultaneous mismatches does a single threshold across categories cause?
why: 同一阈值对不同类别必然两头错配：对边界仇恨言论过删（阈值相对它太严，把讽刺/反制言论也删了），对儿童安全又抓不够（阈值相对它太松，漏放了不可接受的内容）。因为各类的代价不对称完全不同，一个阈值无法同时最优。
why_en: A single threshold is simultaneously too strict for borderline hate speech (over-removing satire/counter-speech) and too lax for child safety (under-catching unacceptable content).
options: 对所有类别都恰好最优，没有错配
对边界仇恨言论过删，同时对儿童安全抓不够——两头错配
只对垃圾信息有影响，其它类别不受牵连
会让所有类别都变得过于宽松，漏放增多但不误删
options_en: It is exactly optimal for all categories, with no mismatch.
It over-removes borderline hate speech while under-catching child safety — mismatched on both ends.
It only affects spam and leaves other categories untouched.
It makes every category too lax — more misses but no over-removal.
optionExplanations: 各类代价不对称不同，一个阈值不可能对所有类都最优，这是核心错误认知。
对；同一阈值相对仇恨言论太严（过删边界）、相对儿童安全太松（漏放），一次犯两种错。
单阈值波及所有类别，不是只影响垃圾信息。
单阈值不是一致偏松：它对某些类偏严过删、对另一些类偏松漏放，方向相反。
optionExplanations_en: Categories have different cost asymmetries, so one threshold cannot be optimal for all — the core misconception.
Correct — one threshold is too strict for hate speech (over-removing borderline) and too lax for child safety (missing) — two errors at once.
A single threshold affects all categories, not just spam.
It is not uniformly lax: too strict (over-remove) for some, too lax (miss) for others — opposite directions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型分数转成删/留决定的临界值；不同类别应有不同阈值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A decision threshold turns a model score into a remove/keep decision; different categories should use different thresholds.

scenario: 内容上传的那一刻要立即决定放行还是拦下，延迟目标约 200ms（范围 100–500ms），一条有害内容前 10 分钟就可能被看几百万次。
scenario_en: At upload you must instantly decide pass or flag with a ~200ms latency target (100-500ms range); a harmful item can be viewed millions of times in its first 10 minutes.
q: 上传时的实时闸门该用什么模型，为什么不用最强的多模态集成？
q_en: What model should the upload-time real-time gate use, and why not the strongest multimodal ensemble?
why: 实时闸门用轻量分类器，在约 200ms 内 pass/flag：因为上传是同步路径，跑不起重型集成或逐帧视频融合。它牺牲精度换低延迟，把病毒式扩散前的曝光压到最小；flag 的进人工、pass 的进已发布库，后面再由批量集成补查。
why_en: The gate uses a lightweight classifier to pass/flag within ~200ms, because the synchronous upload path cannot afford heavy ensembles or per-frame video fusion, trading accuracy for minimal early exposure.
tradeoff: 轻量闸门（约 200ms·压曝光·精度有限） vs 重型集成（更准·太慢·上传路径扛不住）
options: 上传时就跑最强的多模态集成 + 逐帧视频融合，精度优先
用轻量分类器约 200ms 内 pass/flag，压住扩散前曝光；重型集成留给后续批量补查
上传时不做任何检测，全部交给每天一次的策略扫描
让用户上传后等几分钟，用重型模型算完再决定是否发布
options_en: Run the strongest multimodal ensemble plus per-frame video fusion at upload, prioritizing accuracy.
Use a lightweight classifier to pass/flag within ~200ms, minimizing pre-spread exposure; leave heavy ensembles for later batch sweeps.
Do no detection at upload; leave everything to a once-daily policy sweep.
Make users wait minutes after upload while a heavy model finishes before publishing.
whenOtherWins: 对非实时、可先隔离再审的内容（如后台上传、定时发布），可以放宽延迟、直接上更重的模型，不必用轻量闸门。
whenOtherWins_en: For non-real-time content that can be quarantined before review (background uploads, scheduled posts), relax latency and run a heavier model instead of the light gate.
optionExplanations: 重型集成 + 逐帧融合远超 200ms，会阻塞上传路径，实时闸门根本跑不动。
对；轻量闸门在 200ms 内先拦一道，最小化扩散前曝光，重活交给近实时/每日批量。
完全不实时检测，有害内容会在批量扫描到之前病毒式扩散，代价见前 10 分钟百万曝光。
让用户等几分钟严重伤体验，且大多数安全内容被无谓卡住，得不偿失。
optionExplanations_en: A heavy ensemble plus per-frame fusion far exceeds 200ms and blocks the upload path, so the real-time gate cannot run it.
Correct — the light gate stops a first pass within 200ms, minimizing pre-spread exposure, leaving heavy work to near-real-time/daily batches.
No real-time detection lets harmful content go viral before the batch sweep catches it — see millions of views in 10 minutes.
Making users wait minutes badly hurts UX and needlessly holds most safe content — not worth it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上传瞬间用轻量分类器做 pass/flag 的同步检查，压住扩散前曝光。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A real-time gate is a synchronous lightweight pass/flag check at upload that minimizes pre-spread exposure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过闸门后进入的可见内容库，后续被批量集成再扫描。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The published store holds content that passed the gate, later re-scanned by batch ensembles.

q: 把内容审核的混合时序管线按「从上传到多层补查」的顺序排列：
q_en: Order the moderation hybrid pipeline from upload to layered re-checks:
steps: 上传瞬间：轻量实时闸门约 200ms 内 pass/flag
flag 的进人工审核，pass 的进已发布库
近实时批量：多模态集成每 5–15 分钟重扫已发布内容
每日策略扫描：更新后的模型每天全库扫，抓新定义的违规
why: 分层兜底：实时闸门先压扩散前曝光（轻但快）→ flag 进人工、pass 进库 → 5–15 分钟的近实时批量用重型集成补闸门漏的 → 每日全库扫抓「新政策才定义的」违规。越往后模型越重、延迟越松、覆盖越全。
why_en: Layered defense: the fast light gate cuts pre-spread exposure, flagged goes to review and passed to the store, a 5-15 min batch ensemble catches gate misses, and a daily sweep catches newly-defined violations.
diagram:
flowchart TB U["上传"] --> G["实时闸门 ~200ms"] G -->|flag| H["人工审核"] G -->|pass| P["已发布库"] P --> B["近实时批量 5–15min
多模态集成"] P --> D["每日策略扫描"]

termDefinitions.term: near-real-time batch sweep / 近实时批量扫描
termDefinitions.meaning: 每 5–15 分钟用重型多模态集成对已发布内容重新打分，补实时闸门漏的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A near-real-time batch sweep re-scores published content every 5-15 minutes with a heavy multimodal ensemble to catch gate misses.

termDefinitions.term: daily policy sweep / 每日策略扫描
termDefinitions.meaning: 用更新后的模型每天扫全库，抓住因政策更新才被定义为违规的旧内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A daily policy sweep scans the full store with updated models to catch content newly defined as violating by policy updates.

scenario: 有人主张：既然近实时批量集成更准，干脆去掉实时闸门，全靠每 5–15 分钟的批量扫描。但一条有害内容前 10 分钟能被看几百万次。
scenario_en: Someone argues: since the near-real-time batch ensemble is more accurate, drop the real-time gate and rely only on the 5-15 min batch. But a harmful item gets millions of views in its first 10 minutes.
q: 为什么即便闸门模型更弱，也不能只靠批量扫描？
q_en: Why keep the weaker gate instead of relying on batch alone?
why: 因为病毒式扩散把「只靠批量」的漏检代价放大：有害内容在 5–15 分钟批量扫到它之前，就已经被看几百万次、伤害已经发生。实时闸门虽然模型弱，但它在扩散最猛的头几分钟先拦一道，把曝光压到最小——它存在的理由是时效而非精度。
why_en: Virality amplifies batch-only misses: harmful content is seen millions of times before a 5-15 min sweep catches it, so the weaker gate exists to cut exposure in the critical early minutes.
options: 因为批量集成其实更慢更不准，不如闸门
因为病毒式扩散在批量扫到之前已造成百万曝光，闸门用时效（而非精度）先压住早期扩散
因为批量扫描会漏掉所有图像内容，只能靠闸门
因为闸门比批量集成更省算力，纯粹是成本考虑
options_en: Because the batch ensemble is actually slower and less accurate than the gate.
Because virality causes millions of views before the batch catches it, so the gate cuts early spread with timeliness (not accuracy).
Because batch sweeps miss all image content and only the gate handles it.
Because the gate is cheaper than the batch ensemble — purely a cost concern.
optionExplanations: 批量集成其实更准，只是有延迟；闸门的价值不是更准而是更快。
对；扩散最猛的头几分钟里，闸门先拦一道把曝光压到最小，批量再在几分钟后补更准的判定。
批量集成正是多模态、能处理图像，说它漏掉所有图像不成立。
闸门存在的首要理由是压住扩散前曝光的时效，不是省算力。
optionExplanations_en: The batch ensemble is actually more accurate, just delayed; the gate's value is speed, not accuracy.
Correct — in the fiercest early minutes the gate cuts exposure first, and the batch adds a more accurate verdict minutes later.
The batch ensemble is multimodal and handles images, so claiming it misses all images is false.
The gate's primary reason is timeliness to cut pre-spread exposure, not saving compute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容在极短时间内被大量转发/观看，使漏检的早期曝光代价被急剧放大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Virality is content spreading to huge view counts in minutes, sharply amplifying the exposure cost of a missed item.

scenario: 面试官要你说清实时闸门和近实时批量扫描各自的定位。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to contrast the roles of the real-time gate and the near-real-time batch sweep.
q: 实时闸门与近实时批量扫描的核心分工是什么？
q_en: What is the core division of labor between the gate and the batch sweep?
why: 闸门=低延迟、轻模型、在上传瞬间压住扩散前曝光，容忍较低精度；批量=高延迟(5–15min)、重型多模态集成、追高精度补闸门漏检。取舍轴是「时效 vs 精度」：闸门抢时间，批量抢准度，两者叠加。
why_en: The gate is low-latency, lightweight, cutting pre-spread exposure at upload with lower accuracy; the batch is delayed (5-15 min), heavy and multimodal, chasing accuracy to catch gate misses.
tradeoff: 实时闸门（低延迟·轻·压曝光） vs 批量扫描（高延迟·重·高精度补漏）
options: 闸门追高精度、批量追低延迟，分工正好相反
闸门低延迟轻模型压扩散前曝光，批量高延迟重型集成高精度补漏，取舍是时效 vs 精度
两者完全相同，只是部署在不同机房
闸门只处理文本、批量只处理图像，按模态分工
options_en: The gate chases accuracy and the batch chases low latency — roles reversed.
The gate is low-latency and lightweight to cut pre-spread exposure; the batch is delayed and heavy for high-accuracy catch-up — timeliness vs accuracy.
They are identical, just deployed in different datacenters.
The gate handles only text and the batch only images — split by modality.
optionExplanations: 说反了：追精度的是批量、追低延迟的是闸门。
对；闸门抢时间压早期曝光、批量抢准度补漏，二者沿「时效 vs 精度」轴互补。
两者延迟、模型重量、职责都不同，不是同一层换机房。
闸门和批量都是多模态审核，不是按文本/图像切分职责。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed: the batch chases accuracy and the gate chases low latency.
Correct — the gate grabs time to cut early exposure, the batch grabs accuracy to catch misses, complementary along timeliness vs accuracy.
They differ in latency, model weight, and role — not the same layer in a different datacenter.
Both gate and batch are multimodal; they are not split by text vs image.

termDefinitions.meaning: 融合文本/图像/视频/音频多路模型的集成，精度高但重、有延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A multimodal ensemble fuses text/image/video/audio models — high accuracy but heavy and slower.

scenario: 为实时闸门定延迟目标，团队讨论约 200ms（范围 100–500ms）意味着什么设计约束。
scenario_en: Setting the real-time gate's latency target, the team discusses what ~200ms (100-500ms range) implies as a design constraint.
q: 约 200ms 是怎么来的，它约束了闸门能用什么模型？
q_en: Where does ~200ms come from, and what does it constrain about the gate's model?
why: 约 200ms 是给定的产品/服务目标（上传路径可接受的同步延迟），不是公式推出来的。它直接排除了重型多模态集成和逐帧视频融合这类耗时做法，逼你在闸门上用蒸馏/轻量分类器；更准的模型只能挪到延迟宽松的批量层。
why_en: ~200ms is a given product/serving target for the synchronous upload path, not a formula, and it rules out heavy ensembles or per-frame video fusion, forcing a lightweight classifier at the gate.
options: 约 200ms 是给定的产品目标，排除了重型集成/逐帧视频融合，闸门只能用轻量分类器
约 200ms 是由并发量除以 QPS 算出的公式结果
约 200ms 说明闸门可以放心跑最重的多模态模型
约 200ms 只是随便定的，对模型选择没有任何约束
options_en: ~200ms is a given product target that rules out heavy ensembles/per-frame video fusion, so the gate uses a lightweight classifier.
~200ms is a formula result from concurrency divided by QPS.
~200ms means the gate can safely run the heaviest multimodal model.
~200ms is arbitrary and constrains model choice not at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级目标：给定的延迟/可用性目标（如约 200ms），是约束而非推导结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a given latency/availability target (e.g. ~200ms) that acts as a constraint, not a derived result.

scenario: 政策团队新增了一类违规定义（比如某种新型误导内容），而这类内容之前已经发布在库里。
scenario_en: The policy team adds a new violation definition (e.g. a new kind of misleading content), and such content was already published in the store.
q: 每日策略扫描（daily policy sweep）解决的是哪个独特问题？
q_en: What unique problem does the daily policy sweep solve?
why: 它专抓「按旧政策合规、按新政策违规」的存量内容：政策一更新，用更新后的模型每天把全库重扫一遍，把过去漏网、如今被重新定义为违规的内容捞出来。实时闸门和 5–15 分钟批量只覆盖新上传/近期内容，管不了这类回溯。
why_en: It catches back-catalog content that was compliant under old policy but violates the new one, by re-scanning the full store daily with updated models, which the gate and 5-15 min batch (recent content only) cannot do.
options: 降低实时闸门的延迟
回溯存量内容：政策更新后每天全库重扫，抓出如今被重新定义为违规的旧内容
替代人工审核，去掉人在环
只用来统计每天新增内容的数量
options_en: Lower the real-time gate's latency.
Re-check the back catalog: after a policy update, re-scan the full store daily to catch old content newly defined as violating.
Replace human review and remove the human-in-the-loop.
Merely count how much new content is added daily.
optionExplanations: 策略扫描是离线全库任务，不影响也不用于降低闸门延迟。
对；它回溯扫全库，专门抓政策更新后被重新定义为违规的存量内容，是闸门/近实时批量覆盖不到的。
它是自动化补查，不替代人工审核，人在环仍处理边界与申诉。
它的目的是重扫合规性，不是统计新增量。
optionExplanations_en: The policy sweep is an offline full-store job that neither affects nor is used to lower gate latency.
Correct — it re-scans the whole store to catch back-catalog content newly defined as violating after a policy update, which the gate/near-real-time batch cannot cover.
It is automated catch-up, not a replacement for human review; humans still handle borderline and appeals.
Its purpose is re-checking compliance, not counting new volume.

termDefinitions.meaning: 早已发布在库里的历史内容，政策更新后可能需要按新定义重新审。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The back catalog is already-published historical content that may need re-review under a new policy definition.

scenario: 违规形态一直演变（新型仇恨黑话、新型误导），你不想每出现一种新违规就把审核模型从头全量重训。
scenario_en: Violation patterns keep evolving (new hate slang, new misinformation), and you don't want to fully retrain the moderation model from scratch for each new type.
q: 为快速对齐演变中的政策，越来越多用什么手段？
q_en: To align quickly with evolving policy, what approach is increasingly used?
why: 越来越多用强化学习（RL）把审核模型对齐到演变中的政策：用政策反馈作为奖励信号增量调整，能更快适应新违规类型，而不必每次都全量重训。它补的是「政策漂移」下的快速适应能力。
why_en: Reinforcement learning is increasingly used to align moderation models with evolving policy, adapting to new violation types faster than full retraining.
tradeoff: RL 对齐（快速适应政策漂移·实现复杂） vs 每次全量重训（简单直接·慢、成本高）
options: 每出现一种新违规就把模型从头全量重训
用强化学习(RL)按政策反馈增量对齐模型，更快适应新违规类型，免去每次全量重训
冻结模型永不更新，靠人工规则手动打补丁
把所有新违规都当噪声忽略，等积累够多再说
options_en: Fully retrain the model from scratch for each new violation type.
Use reinforcement learning (RL) to incrementally align the model to policy feedback, adapting to new violations faster and skipping full retrains.
Freeze the model forever and patch manually with human rules.
Ignore all new violations as noise until enough accumulate.
whenOtherWins: 当违规定义稳定、训练数据充足、且需要可复现的确定性行为时，定期全量重训比 RL 更简单可控。
whenOtherWins_en: When violation definitions are stable, data is plentiful, and reproducible deterministic behavior matters, periodic full retraining is simpler and more controllable than RL.
optionExplanations: 每次全量重训太慢太贵，追不上违规形态周级演变的速度。
对；RL 用政策反馈做奖励增量对齐，快速适应新违规，是应对政策漂移的主流方向。
冻结 + 手工打补丁扩展性差，跟不上新型黑话/误导的演变。
忽略新违规等于放任有害内容演变期无人管，风险不可接受。
optionExplanations_en: Full retraining each time is too slow and costly to keep up with weekly-evolving violation patterns.
Correct — RL incrementally aligns via policy-feedback reward, adapting fast to new violations — the mainstream answer to policy drift.
Freeze-plus-manual-patch scales poorly and lags evolving slang/misinformation.
Ignoring new violations leaves harmful content unmanaged during its evolution — unacceptable risk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 强化学习：用奖励信号（这里是政策反馈）优化模型行为，支持增量对齐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RL (Reinforcement Learning) optimizes model behavior via reward signals (here policy feedback), enabling incremental alignment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 违规定义和形态随时间演变，使静态训练集快速过时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Policy drift is the evolution of violation definitions and patterns over time, quickly staling a static training set.

scenario: 面试评级：L4 只给「文本仇恨言论微调 BERT + 固定阈值 + 单个实时分类器」，你想答到 Staff+。
scenario_en: Interview leveling: L4 gives 'fine-tune BERT for text hate speech + fixed threshold + single real-time classifier'. You want to answer at Staff+.
q: 从 L5 到 Staff+，内容审核答题的关键升级是什么？
q_en: From L5 to Staff+, what is the key upgrade in a moderation answer?
why: 关键是把审核框成一个「政策/ML/运营协同演化」的社会技术系统：政策操作化是政策/法务/ML 的跨职能工作、类别专用架构缓解 predictive multiplicity、用 RL 应对政策漂移、按类别做平台级 FPR/FNR 看板、跨文本/图像/视频/音频扩到十亿级。不是多堆组件，而是把三方协同和可度量治理讲清楚。
why_en: Frame moderation as a sociotechnical system where policy, ML, and ops co-evolve — cross-functional policy operationalization, category-specific architectures, RL for drift, per-category FPR/FNR dashboards — not just more components.
tradeoff: Staff+（社会技术系统·三方协同·可度量治理） vs L5（多类别+人审升级·仍偏纯技术）
options: Staff+ 就是把模型换成更大的 transformer
把审核框成政策/ML/运营协同演化的社会技术系统：跨职能操作化、类别架构、RL 抗漂移、平台级 FPR/FNR 看板
Staff+ 只要多背几个有害类别的名字
Staff+ 应避免谈政策和运营，专注纯模型指标
options_en: Staff+ just swaps in a bigger transformer.
Frame moderation as a sociotechnical system where policy/ML/ops co-evolve: cross-functional operationalization, category architectures, RL for drift, platform-wide per-category FPR/FNR dashboards.
Staff+ just means memorizing more harm-category names.
Staff+ should avoid policy and ops and focus on pure model metrics.
optionExplanations: 换更大模型是 L4/L5 的组件思维，触不到政策/运营协同这层。
对；Staff+ 的差异化在把审核当社会技术系统讲：跨职能操作化、类别架构抗多重性、RL 抗漂移、可度量治理。
背类别名字是知识点罗列，不是系统级框架能力。
回避政策/运营恰恰丢掉了 Staff+ 最看重的社会技术协同视角。
optionExplanations_en: A bigger model is L4/L5 component thinking that never reaches policy/ops co-evolution.

Correct — the Staff+ differentiator is framing moderation as a sociotechnical system: cross-functional operationalization, category architectures against multiplicity, RL against drift, measurable governance.
Memorizing category names is fact-listing, not system-level framing.
Avoiding policy/ops drops exactly the sociotechnical co-evolution view Staff+ prizes most.

termDefinitions.meaning: 政策、法务、ML 等多团队协同定义边界与执法标准，而非 ML 单方决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-functional means policy, legal, and ML teams jointly define boundaries and enforcement, not ML alone.

scenario: 你想用一个直觉类比向面试官解释审核里 FP/FN 的代价不对称。
scenario_en: You want one intuitive analogy to explain FP/FN cost asymmetry to the interviewer.
q: 医院分诊类比里，FP 和 FN 分别对应什么？
q_en: In the hospital-triage analogy, what do FP and FN map to?
why: 分诊类比：把健康的人送进 ICU（FP，误删好内容）浪费资源、制造摩擦但不致命；把危重病人放回家（FN，放过有害内容）可能致命。这个类比一句话点出「两类错误代价性质不同」，正是要按类别设不同操作点的直觉来源。
why_en: Triage: sending a healthy person to the ICU (FP) wastes resources but is not fatal, while sending a critically ill patient home (FN) can be fatal — the intuition behind asymmetric costs.
options: FP=危重病人放回家、FN=健康人进 ICU，两者对应正好相反
FP=健康人被送进 ICU（浪费资源、不致命）；FN=危重病人被放回家（可能致命）
FP 和 FN 都对应把病人放回家，没有区别
分诊类比说明两类错误代价相同，都该同等对待
options_en: FP = critically ill sent home, FN = healthy sent to ICU — reversed.
FP = a healthy person sent to the ICU (wastes resources, not fatal); FN = a critically ill patient sent home (can be fatal).
Both FP and FN map to sending patients home, with no difference.
The triage analogy says both errors cost the same and deserve equal treatment.
optionExplanations: 对应反了：健康人进 ICU 才是 FP、危重放回家才是 FN。
对；FP 浪费但不致命、FN 可能致命，一句话说清两类错误代价不对称。
两者含义不同，不能都说成放回家。
类比的重点恰恰是两类错误代价不同，不能同等对待。
optionExplanations_en: Mapping reversed: healthy-to-ICU is FP, critically-ill-home is FN.
Correct — FP wastes but is not fatal, FN can be fatal, capturing the asymmetry in one line.
They mean different things and cannot both be 'sent home'.
The analogy's point is exactly that the two errors differ in cost and must not be treated equally.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两类错误(FP/FN)后果轻重不同，需按类别用不同操作点区别对待。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Asymmetric cost means FP and FN have unequal consequences, needing different per-category operating points.

scenario: 面试速记：几个类别的 FP/FN 容忍度与执法取向。
scenario_en: Interview cheat: FP/FN tolerance and enforcement lean for a few categories.
q: 补全各类别的代价取向：
q_en: Fill in each category's cost lean:
text: 儿童安全：FNR 要求{{近零}}，法律/安全压倒创作者摩擦；垃圾信息：可容忍{{高}} FPR 做激进删除（申诉率低）；错误信息：FPR 要{{低}}，倾向{{打标签}}而非直接删除，避免误删合法新闻。
text_en: Child safety: FNR must be {{near-zero}}, legal/safety over creator friction; spam: tolerate {{high}} FPR for aggressive removal (low appeals); misinformation: keep FPR {{low}}, prefer {{labeling}} over removal to avoid deleting legitimate news.
why: 记住方向：儿童安全押 FNR 近零（绝不漏放）、垃圾押 FPR 可高（激进删）、错误信息押 FPR 低 + 打标签（保表达）。每个类别的操作点由它自己的 FP/FN 代价不对称决定，这就是不能用单一阈值的根据。
why_en: Remember the lean: child safety near-zero FNR, spam high FPR tolerance, misinformation low FPR plus labeling — each operating point set by its own cost asymmetry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假阴性率(漏放比例) / 假阳性率(误删比例)，按类别单独设定容忍度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FNR (miss rate) and FPR (wrongful-removal rate) have per-category tolerances.

scenario: 为了压有害内容，你把仇恨言论阈值调得很激进，误删率（FP）明显上升，很多创作者的正常内容被误删。
scenario_en: To suppress harm, you set an aggressive hate-speech threshold; FP rises sharply and many creators' normal content is wrongly removed.
q: FP 升高会触发怎样的二级连锁反应？
q_en: What second-order chain does rising FP trigger?
why: FP 升高 → 创作者信任被侵蚀、他们减少发布 → 平台内容供给下降；同时每次误删都产生一次申诉，吃掉本就紧张的审核人力。所以 FP 不只是「一条内容错删」，它顺着「信任→供给→申诉负载」放大，是要按类别控 FPR 的经营理由。
why_en: Rising FP erodes creator trust so they post less (supply drops), and each wrongful removal spawns an appeal consuming reviewer capacity — the business reason to control FPR per category.
options: 只是当条内容被删，没有任何后续影响
创作者信任受损→减少发布→供给下降，同时申诉洪水吃掉审核人力
会让有害内容漏放（FN）随之上升
只增加存储成本，与创作者和审核人力无关
options_en: Just that item is removed, with no further effect.
Creator trust erodes so they post less (supply drops), while an appeal flood consumes reviewer capacity.
It causes false negatives (FN) to rise as well.
It only raises storage cost, unrelated to creators or reviewers.
optionExplanations: FP 的伤害是系统性的，不止一条内容——它顺着信任和供给放大。
对；误删→创作者流失→供给下降，加上申诉洪水挤占审核人力，这才是 FP 的真实成本。
FP 和 FN 是相反方向的错误，FP 升高不会直接推高 FN。
FP 的主要代价在创作者信任、供给和申诉人力，不是存储。
optionExplanations_en: FP harm is systemic, not just one item — it amplifies through trust and supply.
Correct — wrongful removal loses creators, cuts supply, and floods appeals that eat reviewer capacity — FP's real cost.
FP and FN are opposite errors; rising FP does not directly raise FN.
FP's main cost is creator trust, supply, and appeal labor, not storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 创作者持续产出内容的意愿与数量；误删过多会让他们减少发布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Creator supply is creators' willingness and volume of content; excessive over-removal makes them post less.

scenario: 被 flag 的内容远多于人工审核产能，你必须给人工队列排优先级。一条边界内容既可能很严重，又可能正在快速扩散。
scenario_en: Flagged content far exceeds human-review capacity, so you must prioritize the review queue. A borderline item may be both severe and spreading fast.
q: 人工审核队列该按什么排序（L5 级答案）？
q_en: How should the human-review queue be ordered (L5-level answer)?
why: 按「严重度 + 传播度（virality）」联合排序：越严重、扩散越快的内容越先审，把有限的人工产能投到伤害潜力最大的内容上。只按时间先到先审会让高危高扩散内容排在一堆低危内容后面，错过遏制窗口。
why_en: Order by severity plus virality, reviewing the most severe and fastest-spreading first, to spend limited reviewer capacity where harm potential is highest.
tradeoff: 按严重度+扩散度排（对齐伤害潜力·需额外信号） vs 先到先审（简单·高危高扩散被埋队尾）
options: 先到先审（FIFO），最公平简单
按严重度 + 传播度（virality）联合排序，把人工产能投到伤害潜力最大的内容
按创作者粉丝数排序，大 V 的内容一律先审
随机抽审，避免任何偏置
options_en: First-in-first-out (FIFO) — fairest and simplest.
Order by severity plus virality, spending reviewer capacity where harm potential is highest.
Order by creator follower count — always review big accounts first.
Review a random sample to avoid any bias.
whenOtherWins: 当所有 flag 内容严重度和扩散度都相近（如单一低危类别的小平台）时，FIFO 反而简单公平、无需额外排序信号。
whenOtherWins_en: When all flagged items have similar severity and spread (e.g. a small single-low-risk-category platform), FIFO is simpler and fair without extra ranking signals.
optionExplanations: FIFO 会把高危、正在病毒扩散的内容排在一堆低危内容后面，错过遏制窗口。
对；严重度 + 扩散度对齐伤害潜力，让有限人工先处理最危险、扩散最快的内容。
只按粉丝数会漏掉小号发布的高危内容，且大 V 的普通内容被过度优先。
随机抽审无法对齐伤害潜力，高危内容可能长期不被审到。
optionExplanations_en: FIFO buries high-risk, virally spreading content behind low-risk items, missing the containment window.
Correct — severity plus virality aligns with harm potential, so limited reviewers handle the most dangerous, fastest-spreading first.
Follower count alone misses high-risk content from small accounts and over-prioritizes big accounts' ordinary posts.
Random sampling cannot align with harm potential, so high-risk content may go long unreviewed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条违规内容潜在伤害的大小，用于人工审核队列优先级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Severity is the potential harm magnitude of a violating item, used to prioritize the human-review queue.

scenario: 要给「图像/视频里的血腥暴力」这一类选主判定信号，而仇恨言论那一类主要靠语言。
scenario_en: Choosing the main signal for 'graphic violence in image/video', while the hate-speech category relies mainly on language.
q: 图像血腥暴力类别的主判定信号该落在哪个模态，为什么？
q_en: On which modality should graphic-violence detection primarily rely, and why?
why: 主要靠视觉特征（图像/视频帧），因为血腥暴力是视觉呈现的，文本描述常常缺失或误导。这正是「一个通用文本分类器盖不住所有类别」的具体例证：仇恨言论押语言、图像暴力押视觉，各类主模态不同，驱动类别专用架构。
why_en: Primarily visual features (image/video frames), because graphic violence is visually presented and text is often absent or misleading — an example of why categories need different modalities.
tradeoff: 视觉为主（贴合血腥的视觉本质） vs 文本为主（对图像暴力信号缺失/误导）
options: 主要靠文本，用配文关键词判断是否血腥
主要靠视觉特征（图像/视频帧），因为血腥暴力是视觉呈现的、文本常缺失或误导
主要靠音频，用背景音判断暴力
主要靠发帖时间和地理位置元数据
options_en: Mainly text — judge gore by caption keywords.
Mainly visual features (image/video frames), because graphic violence is visually presented and text is often absent or misleading.
Mainly audio — judge violence by background sound.
Mainly posting time and geolocation metadata.
whenOtherWins: 当暴力主要以口述/音频呈现（如音频里的威胁、枪声）时，音频信号才成为该样本的主判定依据；模态选择跟着内容形态走。
whenOtherWins_en: When violence is presented mainly via speech/audio (spoken threats, gunshots), audio becomes the primary signal — modality follows content form.
optionExplanations: 靠配文关键词会被无文本或误导性配文的血腥内容绕过，抓不到视觉本体。
对；血腥暴力本质是视觉的，主判定落在图像/视频帧，这也是类别专用架构的直接理由。
音频只是辅助信号，静态血腥图像根本没有音频可依。
时间/地理元数据不含内容有害性信号，判不了是否血腥。
optionExplanations_en: Caption keywords are bypassed by gory content with no text or misleading captions, missing the visual substance.
Correct — graphic violence is inherently visual, so the primary signal is image/video frames — a direct reason for category-specific architectures.
Audio is only an auxiliary signal; a static gory image has no audio to rely on.
Time/geo metadata carries no harm signal and cannot judge gore.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容的信号类型：文本、图像、视频、音频；不同有害类别主模态不同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A modality is a content signal type — text, image, video, audio; harm categories differ in their primary modality.
